cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to Titus, his true child in the faith (Titus 1:1, 4). Paul left Titus on the island of Crete to set things in order, and some people there teach things they should not, so Titus has his hands FULL (Titus 1:5, 11). Now Paul tells him, "But as for you…"

cards.question: With those teachers running around Crete, what does Paul tell Titus to speak?

answers.text: Things the crowds want to hear
Things the town elders voted on

cards.text: Now Paul goes down the line like a coach at halftime, one player at a time. First up, the older men: temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance.
The older women are next. Paul wants them reverent in their behavior, not slanderers or addicted to much wine, but teachers of good.

cards.question: Paul says the older women are to be teachers of good. That way they can train the ___ women.

cards.text: The older women can train the young women to love their husbands and children, and to be self-controlled, pure, managers of their households, kind, and submissive to their own husbands.

cards.question: Paul gives a reason for how the young women should live. What is it?

answers.text: So the word of God won't be discredited
So the church in Crete will grow larger
So their households will be admired in town

cards.question: Paul's word for the younger men is much shorter than his word for the older men.

cards.text: Titus is to urge the younger men to be self-controlled. Then Paul turns to Titus himself, and friend, Titus can't be THAT boss who says "we're all in this together" and then leaves at noon.

cards.question: Paul tells Titus how to lead the believers in Crete. What is Titus to show himself to be?
Paul says Titus only needs to be an example in the big things.

cards.text: Titus is to do good works, and in his teaching show integrity, dignity, and wholesome speech that is above reproach. Clean every time, not blurry like my stamps back when my edges were worn down.

cards.question: Paul wants Titus's teaching to be above reproach. What will that do to anyone who opposes them?

answers.text: Leave them ashamed with nothing bad to say
Win them over to the faith right away
Drive them off the island of Crete

cards.text: Next on Paul's list for Titus: slaves. They are to submit to their own masters in everything, be well-pleasing, and not be argumentative.

cards.question: Paul says slaves may take a little from their masters as long as they work hard.

cards.text: Instead, they're to show all good faith. And just like with the young women, Paul tacks on a WHY.

cards.question: Paul gives a reason slaves should show all good faith. What does he say it will do for the teaching about God our Savior?

answers.text: Make it beautiful in every way

cards.text: Then Paul drops the big one: "For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone." EVERYONE, friend, even a stamper from the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul says the grace of God doesn't only bring salvation. It instructs us too. What does it teach us to renounce?
Grace teaches us to wait until a later age to live sensible, upright and godly lives.

cards.text: Living godly lives right now isn't the whole picture, because Paul says we're waiting too. And friend, this isn't waiting on hold with a phone company, because this wait comes with a HOPE.

cards.question: Paul says we await the blessed hope and a glorious appearance. Whose appearance are we waiting for?

cards.text: Paul calls Jesus "our great God and Savior Jesus Christ." Nobody's told me the day, friend, so I keep my ovens HOT.

cards.question: Paul says Jesus gave Himself for us, to redeem us from all ___.

cards.text: Somebody once bought me out of a bakery's clearance bin for 25 cents, and Jesus gave HIMSELF, friend. He did it to purify for Himself a people for His own possession.

cards.question: Jesus purifies a people for His own possession. What does Paul say those people are zealous for?

cards.text: Paul wraps up with one last word for Titus: speak these things, with all authority.

cards.question: Paul tells Titus to rebuke, not only to encourage.
Titus is to speak with all authority. Paul tells him to let no one ___ him.
